title: Strings, Bytes, and encoding
preamble:
# Strings, Bytes, and encoding

The `String` and `Bytes` slot types and
the contract on how they relate. DS strings are Unicode; bytes
are byte sequences; conversion between them is explicit.

Paired with:
- [LLEX] for string-literal lexical syntax.
- [LEXP] for string operations
  (interpolation, ordering, regex and the rest).
- [LFAC] for slot-type declarations.
- [LADP] for adapter-side
  obligations on String / Bytes wire data.

## What this is not

- Not a string-operation library spec. Operations live in
  [LEXP]; this doc only fixes the
  underlying type semantics.
- Not a Unicode normalisation spec. Comparison is by codepoint
  sequence; normalisation forms (NFC, NFD, NFKC, NFKD) are not
  applied implicitly.
- Not a locale spec. String operations are locale-agnostic; no
  locale-aware comparison, casing, or sorting.
